title: Musée Condé: Masterpieces
subtitle: Twenty paintings at the Musée Condé, where an object in the hand can change the meaning of a figure.
introduction:
Marie-Antoinette holds the attributes of Hebe without ceasing to look like a court sitter. Nearby in this selection, a woman traditionally identified as Simonetta Vespucci is given a serpent, but no fully secure name. A likeness can be specific while the identity or role attached to it remains complicated.

The Musée Condé's paintings make such distinctions worth keeping. Their figures act as saints, mythological beings, military leaders, musicians and named individuals. Sometimes a small gesture is enough to organise the image: lifting a veil, withholding a bow or raising a hand. The twenty entries follow these actions, while preserving the difference between an original painting, a sketch and an uncertain identification.
visitNote: Check the Château de Chantilly's visitor pages for gallery access and temporary changes. This guide identifies works in the collection and does not guarantee that every object will be on view.

books.title: A Treatise on Painting
books.author: Leonardo da Vinci; translated by John Francis Rigaud
books.note: Leonardo's Treatise on Painting, in an English translation, discusses gesture, light and the observation of bodies. Those topics provide a useful historical reading alongside the figures by Raphael, Piero di Cosimo and Ingres, without implying that each followed the treatise.

works.title: The Madonna of Loreto
works.credit: Raphael. LA VIERGE DE LORETTE. WikiArt: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop.
works.description: The veil joins two movements: Mary's careful lifting and the child's reaching arms. Joseph remains farther back in shadow, watching an action that brings the foreground figures together. The sacred family is organised around this small material connection. The cloth can be thin and almost transparent while still providing the group's most consequential link.

works.title: Portrait of a Woman, Said to Be Simonetta Vespucci
works.catalogueTitle: Portrait of a Woman, said to be of Simonetta Vespucci
works.credit: Piero di Cosimo. Portrait of a Woman, said to be of Simonetta Vespucci. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The precise profile gives the sitter an apparently stable identity, then the serpent and dark clouds complicate it. The traditional name Simonetta Vespucci remains qualified, and the attributes should not be used to make that identification certain. Portrait-like specificity and uncertainty about who is represented are both part of looking at this work.

works.title: Self-Portrait at the Age of Twenty-Four
works.credit: Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres. Self-Portrait at the Age of 24. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/jean-auguste-dominique-ingres/self-portrait-at-the-age-of-24
works.description: The painter turns from his task and meets the outward view, bringing work and self-presentation into the same pose. His pale shirt separates the upper body from the dark coat. The interruption is constructed within a self-portrait: the person who seems to have paused is also responsible for arranging the encounter.

works.title: Madame Antonia de Vauçay, Born de Nittis
works.catalogueTitle: Portrait of Madame Antonia de Vaucay nee de Nittis
works.credit: Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres. Portrait of Madame Antonia de Vaucay nee de Nittis. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/jean-auguste-dominique-ingres/portrait-of-madame-antonia-de-vaucay-nee-de-nittis-1807
works.description: Joined hands rest within the larger enclosure of dress, shawl and chair. The red furniture gives the seated body a firmer boundary, while the hands offer a quieter internal centre. Ingres holds the portrait together through these nested curves, allowing a slight change in face or posture to matter within a controlled arrangement.

works.title: Venus Anadyomene
works.credit: Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres. VENUS ANADYOMENE. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The long pale body holds a sustained pose above much smaller winged figures. The extended development of the painting also matters: Ingres began the project during his early years in Rome and completed it in 1848. Its apparent stillness is the product of prolonged work, not evidence that the whole design arrived at once.

works.title: Five Dancing Angels
works.credit: Giovanni di Paolo. CINQ ANGES DANSANT. Image credit: Giovanni di Paolo; Own work , Jebulon , 2011-07-03. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Angels_dancing_sun_Giovanni_di_Paolo_Cond%C3%A9_Chantilly.jpg. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression; applicable ShareAlike terms retained.
works.description: The joined hands make a continuous connection through the five bodies, including those whose backs turn outward. Folds and alternating poses give the group movement against gold without a deep space into which they can travel. The dance is read through repeated changes of orientation within the circle itself.

works.title: The Serenader
works.credit: The Serenader. WikiArt; Jean-Antoine Watteau. Proportional resizing and JPEG compression; source frame preserved.
works.description: The crossed legs and the instrument's diagonal give the musician a pose that seems already shaped by performance. Costume frames the face but does not carry the action alone. Watteau makes the body participate in the music, allowing a silent picture to describe something of playing through stance and direction.

works.title: Love Disarmed
works.credit: Antoine Watteau. L'AMOUR DESARME. WikiArt: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop.
works.description: Cupid reaches for a bow held beyond him. The modest gap between hand and object supplies the whole exchange with its action, while the oval keeps the two bodies close. An allegory of disarmed love is made legible through a familiar imbalance: one figure can possess what the other wants but cannot yet reach.

works.title: Horse Leaving a Stable
works.credit: Horse leaving a Stable. WikiArt; Théodore Géricault. Proportional resizing and JPEG compression; source frame preserved.
works.description: The lifted foreleg places the horse between standing and moving out of the stable. A nearby handler shares that narrow threshold, while light distinguishes the animal's weight from the darker doorway. The scene depends on this unresolved transition; it would change substantially if the horse were already in an open landscape.

works.title: A Pyrenean Shepherd
works.credit: Rosa Bonheur. Berger des Pyrénées. Image credit: Rosa Bonheur; Own work; Photographic credit: Dguendel. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Ch%C3%A2teau_de_Chantilly,_Rosa_Bonheur,_sheeps_in_the_Pyrenees.JPG. CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression; applicable ShareAlike terms retained.
works.description: The staff, animals and rough ground define a shared working environment. The shepherd does not appear simply to ornament a mountain view, and the animals are not interchangeable patches of rural colour. Differences of posture and texture make their relation to the terrain specific enough to sustain the picture without a dramatic event.

works.title: The Childhood of Bacchus
works.credit: Nicolas Poussin. Nurture of Bacchus. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/nicolas-poussin/nurture-of-bacchus-1635
works.description: The infant occupies a gathering broken into smaller relations among figures and satyrs. Gestures connect these episodes across the woodland setting, so the myth can be followed without every body merging into a crowd. Poussin gives the scene a readable social organisation before each participant's identity has been established.

works.title: The Christ Child, Saviour of the World
works.credit: Bernardino Luini. L'ENFANT JESUS, SAUVEUR DU MONDE. Image credit: Bernardino Luini; Own work; Photographic credit: Dguendel. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Ch%C3%A2teau_de_Chantilly,_Bernardino_Luini,_Jesu_as_a_child.JPG. CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression; applicable ShareAlike terms retained.
works.description: The child's small body is accompanied by a raised hand, cross-staff and orb, signs whose claims exceed his physical scale. Their separation makes that difference legible. The image joins infancy to spiritual authority rather than asking one to cancel the other; the clear silhouette keeps both present.

works.title: Esther Chosen by Ahasuerus
works.credit: Filippino Lippi. Esther choisie par Assuérus. WikiArt: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop.
works.description: Arcades divide the wide panel into connected spaces, giving the courtly story more than one place to unfold. Bright clothing distinguishes groups within this repeated architecture. The royal throne supplies a focus, but the panel's breadth allows attention to travel between participants rather than stopping permanently at one central figure.

works.title: Count Henri de Bergh
works.catalogueTitle: PORTRAIT DU COMTE HENRI DE BERGHE
works.credit: Anthony van Dyck. PORTRAIT DU COMTE HENRI DE BERGHE. Image credit: Anthony van Dyck; Base Joconde. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Portrait_du_comte_Henri_de_Berghe_-_Anton_van_Dyck_-_Mus%C3%A9e_Cond%C3%A9.jpg. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression; applicable ShareAlike terms retained.
works.description: Armour makes much of the body appear enclosed and resistant, while the face and hand remain comparatively exposed. The hand's position near the sword joins those living features to military equipment. Van Dyck presents rank through a composed arrangement, giving its wearer an individual presence without stripping away the role that clothing declares.

works.title: Marie-Antoinette as Hebe
works.catalogueTitle: Madame la Dauphine Marie-Antoinette, en Hébé
works.credit: François-Hubert Drouais. Madame la Dauphine Marie-Antoinette, en Hébé. Image credit: François-Hubert Drouais; Jebulon ( talk · contribs ) (2011). https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Marie_Antoinette_dauphine_H%C3%A9b%C3%A9_Drouais_Chantilly.jpg. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression; applicable ShareAlike terms retained.
works.description: The jug and eagle identify Hebe, while the face and elaborately dressed hair preserve the conventions of a royal portrait. Marie-Antoinette is therefore represented in a role, not replaced by an anonymous mythological figure. The costume offers a classical framework through which a specific public identity can be presented.

works.title: The Ham Luncheon
works.credit: Nicolas Lancret. LE DEJEUNER DE JAMBON. Image credit: Nicolas Lancret; Joconde database :  entry 00000076666. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:D%C3%A9jeuner_de_jambon_-_Nicolas_Lancret_-_mus%C3%A9e_Cond%C3%A9.jpg. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression; applicable ShareAlike terms retained.
works.description: The white tablecloth gathers the meal into one bright area, but bottles below and gestures around it keep the company from settling into a formal group portrait. The park provides room for sociability to spread. Several small exchanges can coexist without one diner being made the unquestioned centre of the occasion.

works.title: Bonaparte Visiting the Plague-Stricken at Jaffa: Chantilly Version
works.catalogueTitle: BONAPARTE, GENERAL EN CHEF DE L'ARMEE D'ORIENT, TOUCHE UNE TUMEUR PESTILENTIELLE, EN VISITANT LES PESTIFERES DANS L'HOPITAL DE JAFFA
works.credit: Antoine-Jean Gros. BONAPARTE, GENERAL EN CHEF DE L'ARMEE D'ORIENT, TOUCHE UNE TUMEUR PESTILENTIELLE, EN VISITANT LES PESTIFERES DANS L'HOPITAL DE JAFFA. Image credit: Antoine-Jean Gros; Own work , Pierre Poschadel , 2019-09-22. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Chantilly_(60),_mus%C3%A9e_Cond%C3%A9,_Antoine_Jean_Baron_Gros,_Bonaparte_et_les_pestif%C3%A9r%C3%A9s_de_Jaffa,_1804.jpg. CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/). Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression; applicable ShareAlike terms retained.
works.description: Bonaparte's approach to the sick is made conspicuous within the arcaded enclosure. Light separates bodies and turns the act into a public presentation of leadership. The Chantilly work is catalogued as a sketch related to the larger Louvre painting; it should be read as its own object, not treated as an interchangeable reproduction of that version.

works.title: In the Abruzzi
works.credit: Oswald Achenbach. DANS LES ABRUZZES. Image credit: Oswald Achenbach; Own work , 2017-08-30, Dguendel. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Ch%C3%A2teau_de_Chantilly,_Oswald_Achenbach,_in_the_Abruzzo.JPG. CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression; applicable ShareAlike terms retained.
works.description: A roadside shrine gives the travellers a reason to stop while the road continues toward distant mountains. The landscape contains both pause and passage, measured by figures at different distances. The journey is organised through places that can be occupied briefly, rather than through an uninterrupted prospect seen from outside human use.

works.title: Heron Hunt in Algeria
works.credit: Eugène Fromentin. LA CHASSE AU HERON (ALGERIE). Image credit: Eugène Fromentin; Jebulon , Own work. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Chasse_au_h%C3%A9ron_Fromentin_Mus%C3%A9e_Cond%C3%A9.jpg. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression; applicable ShareAlike terms retained.
works.description: The hunters remain widely separated across shallow water, with birds and riders interrupting a low horizon. That spacing makes distance part of the action: the hunt cannot be reduced to one close encounter. The large sky also keeps the figures within an extensive setting instead of allowing their movement to fill the whole picture.

works.title: The Angel Gabriel with Musical Angels and Cherubs
works.catalogueTitle: L'ANGE GABRIEL DANS UNE GLOIRE D'ANGES MUSICIENS ET DE CHERUBINS
works.credit: Annibale Carracci. L'ANGE GABRIEL DANS UNE GLOIRE D'ANGES MUSICIENS ET DE CHERUBINS. Image credit: Annibale Carracci; Joconde database :  entry 00000077351. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Annibale_Carracci,_Arcangelo_Gabriele,_Museo_Cond%C3%A9.jpg. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression; applicable ShareAlike terms retained.
works.description: Gabriel's open arms give the surrounding ascent a clear point of attention. Blue and red clothing distinguish the central body, while smaller angels and clouds continue the movement around it. The heavenly gathering is held together through direction and colour rather than a ground plane on which all the figures could stand.

closingSections.title: Keep the object distinct from its story
paragraphs: A familiar subject may survive in several versions, and a traditional name may be less certain than a face appears. Use the linked records to keep those distinctions clear. Consult the château's current visiting information separately; this selection does not specify a route or guarantee the availability of every object.
